sanskrit_verse: आक्षिप्तमोघबीजाभ्यां पत्यौ अप्रतिकर्मणि । पतिरन्यः स्मृतो नार्याः वत्सरं संप्रतीक्ष्य तु ॥
transliteration: ākṣiptamoghabījābhyāṁ patyau apratikarmaṇi | patir anyaḥ smṛto nāryāḥ vatsaraṁ saṁpratīkṣya tu ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When a husband has cast out his wife or rendered her incapable of bearing fruit, and he performs no restitution, another husband may be lawfully recognized for that woman after one full year.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from capacity to sustain dharma in union
Causation is rooted in the failure to restore relational integrity
Capacity-based responsibility demands completion before replacement
Restoration logic requires temporal thresholds to ensure irreversible intent
Consciousness alignment necessitates acknowledgment of cessation prior to renewal
executable_legal_axioms: IF husband has expelled wife AND performed no restitution within one year THEN wife is eligible for lawful remarriage
IF union is voided by irreversible act AND no compensatory action taken THEN new union recognition is permitted after 360 days
IF marital bond is severed without dharmic completion THEN woman's reproductive and spiritual autonomy must be restored before new union
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating matrimonial dissolution, the Supreme Court must recognize that legal severance occurs not merely by declaration, but by the absence of restorative action over a full cycle of time. The one-year threshold ensures consciousness-level completion and prevents premature legal fragmentation.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that severance is factual when restitution is absent for a full year. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that without restoration, the relational field collapses naturally. Responsibility lies in completing the prior union; the law does not punish but aligns consequence with consciousness.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process: One-year waiting period ensures all restorative avenues are exhausted
Responsibility assumption protocol: Husband must acknowledge severance and either restore or release
Capacity restoration: Woman’s right to form new union activates only after prior union’s irreversible end
Integrity reintegration: Legal system confirms cessation before validating new union
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma prevails through conscious completion, not punitive enforcement. The law serves restoration, not retribution. Reality itself adjudicates through time and intent.
